steps.title: Open a to-do task
steps.body: Click the highlighted card. We're going to stop this task two different ways, and then unstop it. Both mechanisms exist because they model genuinely different situations.

steps.title: Dependencies
steps.body: A dependency says: that other task has to finish before this one can. It's a relationship between two specific pieces of work.

steps.title: Add one
steps.body: Pick any other task in this project from "+ Add blocker…", then press Add. Constellation refuses circular chains, so you can't accidentally build a deadlock.

steps.title: Now try to finish it
steps.body: Set the status to Done. It won't let you — and it tells you which task is in the way. The same check runs on the server, so nobody routes around it by dragging.

steps.title: Take it back off
steps.body: Remove the dependency with the × beside it. Notice the task frees itself immediately — you never have to remember to un-block something by hand.

steps.title: Now a blocker
steps.body: A blocker is different: it's a reusable, project-wide reason — "waiting on the machine shop" — that can sit on many tasks at once. Attach that one from the Blockers section's picker.

steps.title: It moved itself
steps.body: Close the task with the × at the top left of the modal, then look at the board. Attaching a blocker forces the card to BLOCKED — the board can't show something as active while it's stuck.

steps.title: Grouped by reason
steps.body: Blocked cards cluster under the reason blocking them. Which turns "why is nothing moving" into a list of four things somebody needs to go chase.

steps.title: Open it again
steps.body: Click your task inside this bin. Everything about a blocked card is still editable — being blocked is a state, not a lock.

steps.title: Clear it
steps.body: Detach the blocker with the × beside it. The task recomputes: no open blockers and no unfinished dependencies means it goes back to to-do on its own.

steps.title: One level up
steps.body: Dependencies and blockers stop individual tasks. Reports are how you see whether a whole date is in trouble — open the tab and the video after this explains what you're looking at.
